items.headline: CONFIRMED: Iran retaliates for Larak Island strike, hitting Jordan and UAE bases -- last night's unverified claim now multi-sourced
items.summary: NPR, Al Jazeera and The Hill independently confirm Iran's IRGC fired ballistic missiles and drones at Jordan's King Hussein and Al Azraq bases and targeted US forces/helicopters at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in the UAE late Sunday, retaliating for the US strike on Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island -- the first exchange of fire between the two sides in over a month. Jordan's military said it intercepted eight incoming missiles with no reported casualties; the UAE denied Iranian state-media claims that its Al Minhad air base was hit, saying instead it intercepted drones over territorial waters. This resolves yesterday's single-sourced, unconfirmed Fox News claim -- it is now corroborated by wire-quality reporting (NPR/AP-sourced), not one unnamed official.
items.actionable: A real, but so far contained, escalation (all missiles reportedly intercepted, no casualties) -- supportive of a continued haven bid in gold/silver/oil into Tuesday's Asia open, but not yet evidence of a broader regional war that would argue for cutting HK tech or SGX risk.

items.headline: Oil extends gains into Monday close on Jordan/UAE escalation -- Brent near $90, WTI above $86
items.summary: Oil posted its biggest one-day gain in three weeks on Monday as the now-confirmed Iran strikes on Jordan and the UAE raised concern about a prolonged Strait of Hormuz disruption, per Bloomberg's Monday markets wrap. WTI traded above $86/bbl after advancing roughly 2.8% in the prior session, while Brent closed near $90/bbl.
items.actionable: Sustained oil strength keeps the inflation-vs-haven tension for the miners sleeve alive into this week's ISM/NFP prints -- treat as an ongoing risk factor, not a one-off spike that's already fading.

items.headline: Correcting the tape: Friday's Warsh-driven gold/silver rout is a day old, not a Monday event -- watch for an oversized 'Monday' print in the feed
items.summary: Gold fell to roughly $4,470/oz and silver dropped about 3.3% specifically on Friday 28 Aug, in the hours immediately following Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks -- a targeted repricing of the dollar and Treasury yields (2yr +11.8bp to 4.348%) rather than a broad risk-off event, since equities barely moved on the same speech (TipRanks, CNBC). CME futures show Monday itself was comparatively calm for the metals -- gold roughly +0.39%, silver +0.30% on the day. Because the portfolio's price spine is missing a standalone Friday bar, GLD/SLV/GDX and the silver miners are logging both sessions at once under 'Monday' (GLD -3.36%, SLV -4.21%, GDX -5.00% cumulative; MP -7.25%, UUUU -6.29% cumulative) -- a stale Friday reaction, not new Tuesday-morning selling pressure.
items.actionable: Don't read the miners sleeve's large logged drawdown as fresh selling since Monday's close -- it is Friday's Fed-driven repricing catching up in the feed one session late; actual day-shape data (CME futures) shows Monday was flat-to-up.

items.headline: September Fed hike odds harden into a genuine coin-flip on CME and Kalshi
items.summary: CME FedWatch shows September hike odds at roughly 55.7%, about 20 points higher than pre-Warsh levels, while Kalshi prices a 47% hike / 54% hold split. The 2-year Treasury yield has moved up 12bp to 4.35% since Friday's speech -- the biggest jump since Warsh's first hawkish press conference in June.
items.actionable: The hike debate is a real 50/50 market-pricing event into the 16 Sep FOMC, now compounded by today's ISM Manufacturing PMI/JOLTS and Friday's NFP -- size any silver/miner leverage additions with that binary risk explicitly in mind.

items.headline: Silver miners' August rally still outpaces the metal itself despite Friday's Warsh-driven rout
items.summary: Even after Friday's selloff, Hecla Mining is up 47% for August, First Majestic Silver +42%, and Pan American Silver +22% -- all ahead of silver's own monthly gain. The Silver Institute projects a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit for 2026, widening to 46.3m oz, on solar, EV and AI-infrastructure demand.
items.actionable: The structural deficit thesis behind the levered silver/miners sleeve is intact and the monthly trend remains strongly positive despite Friday's single-day shock -- treat Friday as noise within a still-bullish month rather than a trend break.

items.headline: Tencent unveils Hy4 AI model, claims narrow edge over Zhipu's GLM-5.3 and Moonshot's Kimi K3
items.summary: Tencent released and open-sourced Hy4 Preview, a 770-billion-parameter model with a 1-million-token context window, saying internal blind tests show it slightly beating rivals Z.ai and Moonshot on engineering and coding tasks. The company showcased use cases including generating a playable game prototype from a single natural-language prompt, 3D web design, and accounting-compliance workflows, and is integrating the model into its WorkBuddy tool and chatbot.
items.actionable: An incremental positive AI datapoint for a core holding, but China's tech majors remain structurally behind the global AI-hardware trade -- sentiment support for the existing 0700.HK position, not a standalone reason to add size.

items.headline: Xiaomi puts Xring O3 chip into mass production six days after third straight quarter of falling profit
items.summary: Xiaomi's self-designed Xring O3, built by TSMC on a 3nm process with 24bn transistors, entered mass production targeting 200,000-300,000 units for a September foldable launch -- coming just six days after Xiaomi reported Q2 profit down 42.6% on rising component costs. The company has now sunk over 20bn yuan (~US$3bn) into in-house chip development, a bet on supply-chain control rather than near-term cost savings.
items.actionable: Vertical-integration capex during a profit slump is a legitimate long-term-moat story for Xiaomi but a near-term margin drag -- treat as a reason to hold through the earnings weakness rather than a fresh bullish catalyst.

items.headline: SMIC's interim report beats -- revenue +23.1% YoY, net profit +39.8%; shares jump 17.45% (A-share), 10.76% (HK)
items.summary: SMIC's 2026 interim report showed revenue up 23.1% YoY to RMB32.35bn and net profit up 39.8% to RMB2.3bn. The stock rallied 17.45% on the Shanghai market and 10.76% in Hong Kong on the print, pushing total market cap to roughly RMB578.2bn.
items.actionable: A strong fundamental beat for a direct portfolio holding -- the rally has largely already played out, so this is confirmation of the thesis rather than a fresh entry signal.

items.headline: China unveils property-sector reforms: 40-year mortgages, developer fundraising support, pre-sale escrow standards
items.summary: China's central bank will allow mortgages of up to 40 years (from 30), and the CSRC will support developer fundraising via equity and bond sales; new rules also require minimal upfront deposits and let buyers cancel if construction deadlines are missed. The reforms come as consumer spending has slowed and home prices kept falling.
items.actionable: A genuine policy-easing step for China's property sector and broader consumer sentiment -- modestly supportive of the China-risk-appetite backdrop for the HK tech sleeve, though it also underscores how weak underlying property demand still is.

items.headline: JPMorgan downgrades OCBC to underweight, cuts DBS price target to S$63 from S$70
items.summary: JPMorgan downgraded OCBC to underweight (target cut to S$20.50) and lowered DBS's target to S$63 from S$70, while raising SGX's target -- citing asset-quality and geopolitical-risk concerns for the Singapore banking sector, a notable divergence from the sector's record 1H26 income prints.
items.actionable: A direct, negative read on two core portfolio holdings from a major house -- worth weighing against the banks' still-strong 1H26 income and margin data before adding to DBS/OCBC exposure.

items.headline: DBS Research reiterates Buy on Singtel, TP S$5.46, on Optus margin-expansion catalyst
items.summary: DBS maintains a Buy call on Singtel with an unchanged S$5.46 target, flagging management's internal target of OpCo EBIT reaching S$2.1-2.5bn by FY30, driven largely by Optus -- whose EBIT is expected to nearly double from S$488m (FY26) to roughly S$1.0bn by FY30.
items.actionable: A constructive multi-year read on Singtel's largest subsidiary supports the SGX sleeve's income thesis, independent of the Iran/Fed volatility.

items.headline: August set to be first month Ether ETF inflows overtake Bitcoin's; BTC ETFs end 9-day inflow streak with $202M outflow
items.summary: US spot Ether ETFs pulled in $3.87bn in August versus roughly $750m in net Bitcoin ETF outflows for the month -- the first time this has happened. Bitcoin ETFs still logged $924.5m over 24-28 Aug before a $202m outflow on Friday ended a nine-day, $3.04bn inflow streak, while Ether ETFs extended their own inflow streak to 10 straight sessions. Bitcoin itself was consolidating in the high-$76k-78k range into Monday after a brief dip to ~$76,871 on Aug 31.
items.actionable: A genuine rotation signal within crypto (ETH over BTC) rather than a broad risk-off move -- Bitcoin is consolidating rather than breaking down, consistent with a rate-sensitive but not panicked market into the Sep FOMC debate.

items.headline: Lynas misses FY26 profit despite record revenue as non-China rare-earth pricing surges; shares fall 5.9%
items.summary: Lynas Rare Earths, the largest rare-earth refiner outside China, reported record net income of A$222.4m for FY26 (year to June 30) -- up from A$8m a year earlier but below the A$263.2m analyst consensus -- as costs climbed 37% amid a ramp-up of new Australian facilities. Revenue still jumped 76% to A$977.9m on record non-China pricing, but Sydney-listed shares fell 5.9% on the miss. China's rare-earth export curbs on MP Materials and other US/allied firms remain paused through 10 Nov 2026.
items.actionable: Confirms the non-China rare-earth pricing tailwind behind the watchlist thesis is real and accelerating, even as near-term cost/execution risk (Lynas's capex ramp) is the offsetting factor to underwrite before adding size ahead of the Nov 10 export-curb pause expiry.

items.headline: This week's calendar: ISM Manufacturing/JOLTS today, RBNZ decision and ADP Wed, ISM Services Thu, NFP Friday
items.summary: Today (Tue 1 Sep) brings ISM Manufacturing PMI (consensus 55.2 vs prior 55.6) and JOLTS job openings. RBNZ decides Wednesday, with ~90% of economists expecting a 25bp hike to 2.75% from 2.50% amid a split policy committee; ADP jobs also print Wednesday. ISM Services follows Thursday, and Friday brings Non-Farm Payrolls (consensus 55K, a rebound expected after August's -23K).
items.actionable: A genuinely heavy data week stacked on top of the already-live September hike coin-flip -- avoid adding fresh leverage to the metals/miners sleeve until Friday's NFP print clarifies which way the Fed-odds break, rather than reacting to any single day's data.
